clinician.trajectory_summary: A 10-year-old patient presented with a 2-3 month history of vomiting, dizziness, and blurred vision consistent with posterior fossa mass effect and increased intracranial pressure. Imaging identified a posterior fossa mass. Total surgical resection was performed with ventriculoperitoneal shunt insertion. Initial pathology was documented as grade 2 posterior fossa ependymoma (PFE). Adjuvant cranial radiotherapy was administered (50 Gy in 30 fractions). The patient remained well until their late 20s when they experienced acute neurological decline with left-sided weakness and dysphasia due to basilar artery thrombosis, treated with thrombolysis complicated by life-threatening epistaxis, followed by slow recovery over 12 months with residual deficits. Histopathology confirmed the final diagnosis of grade 1 myxopapillary ependymoma with GFAP and EMA positivity.

final.trajectory_summary: A 10-year-old patient presented with a 2-3 month history of vomiting, dizziness, and blurred vision consistent with posterior fossa mass effect and increased intracranial pressure. Imaging identified a posterior fossa mass. Total surgical resection was performed with ventriculoperitoneal shunt insertion. Initial pathology was documented as grade 2 posterior fossa ependymoma (PFE). Adjuvant cranial radiotherapy was administered (50 Gy in 30 fractions). The patient remained well until their late 20s when they experienced acute neurological decline with left-sided weakness and dysphasia due to basilar artery thrombosis, treated with thrombolysis complicated by life-threatening epistaxis, followed by slow recovery over 12 months with residual deficits. Histopathology confirmed the final diagnosis of grade 1 myxopapillary ependymoma with GFAP and EMA positivity.
